classification.difficultyReason: Use the taught circular block method in (a). In (b), compress four couples into units, account for rotational equivalence, and impose Shane and Penny's non-adjacency among the six units before restoring each couple's internal orders.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Five boys and five girls sit around a round table. There are two couples who wish to sit together. How many ways can this be done?

answer.worked:
Treat each couple as one unit. The units are $(BG),(BG),B,B,B,G,G,G$.

There are eight distinct units, so their circular arrangements number $7!$. Each couple can be arranged internally in $2!$ ways.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Number of arrangements}&=7!\times2!\times2!\\&=20\,160.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Five boys and five girls sit around a round table. There are four couples who wish to sit together, and an ex-couple Shane and Penny who do not wish to sit together. How many ways can this be done?

answer.worked:
Treat the four couples as four distinct units. Together with Shane and Penny, the units are $(BG),(BG),(BG),(BG),S,P$.

Fix Shane's position. Of the five remaining unit positions, Penny can occupy three that are not adjacent to Shane. Arrange the four couple units in the remaining positions in $4!$ ways. Each couple has $2!$ internal arrangements.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Number of arrangements}&=1\times3\times4\times3\times2\times1\times(2!)^4\\&=1152.\end{aligned}$$
